title: Directory records can serve as attributable evidence about individuals and relationships
description: Persisted account records and parent-child relationship links can later be used as evidence that a specific student or parent account existed and was associated in a particular way. This may reduce plausible deniability regarding account ownership or asserted family relationships.
assumptions: Assumes stored records are queryable, retained, or auditable in a way that preserves attribution to the linked individuals.
uncertainty_note: There is no explicit mention of signatures or audit logs, so this is limited to attribution arising from the stored data itself.

title: Propagation of student and parent relationship data to the account directory may exceed strict need
description: The grading service propagates account records and parent-child links into the account directory. If the directory does not strictly require full relationship information for its function, this transfer exposes additional personal data to another repository beyond the grading context.
assumptions: Assumes the account directory's core function could be fulfilled with less data than full parent-child linkage details.
uncertainty_note: The necessity of storing parent-child links in the directory is not fully specified; if relationship management is a core purpose of the directory, this threat may be weaker.

title: Data subjects may be unaware that grading operations write family-link data into the directory
description: Students and parents may not reasonably expect that the grading service writes account records and explicit parent-child relationship links into a shared account directory. This creates a risk that data subjects are unaware of the storage and secondary use of their relationship data.
assumptions: Assumes this internal propagation is not clearly communicated to students and parents.
uncertainty_note: Awareness depends on notice provided elsewhere, which is not described in the prompt.

title: Storing relationship-linked account data in the directory may violate data minimization
description: If the account directory receives more account details or family-relationship information than necessary for directory purposes, the write operation may process more personal data than needed. This creates a potential GDPR-style data minimization non-compliance risk.
assumptions: Assumes the directory can function without some of the transferred account or parent-child linkage data.
uncertainty_note: This depends on the directory's actual purpose and lawful design scope, which are not fully specified.

title: Full backup contains persistent account identifiers enabling cross-record linkage
description: The nightly backup ships full grade records, assignments, and the account directory together. Persistent student/account identifiers in the directory and records allow the cloud provider to link multiple records, activities, and historical snapshots to the same individual across datasets and time.

title: Recipient can link individuals through combined educational and directory attributes
description: At the cloud hosting provider, the combination of grade records, assignment data, and account-directory attributes forms a strong quasi-identifier set. Even if some direct identifiers were reduced in parts of the dataset, the combined attributes can still link records belonging to the same person.

title: Backup transfer processes directly identified student and account data
description: The flow explicitly transfers full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to the third-party provider. This indicates processing and disclosure of directly identified personal data, likely including names, usernames, email addresses, or other account references tied to academic records.

title: Academic and directory attributes at the provider reveal identities
description: Once received by the provider, the combination of academic records and directory information contains revealing attributes that support or directly enable identification of individual students and possibly staff.

title: Grade and assignment records constitute attributable evidence about individuals
description: Full grade records and assignment data can be used as attributable evidence about a student's submissions, performance, and account-associated actions. Replicated backups preserve these records in a form that may later be used to prevent denial of those facts or actions.
uncertainty_note: This is a privacy threat because educational records are attributable, but the exact evidentiary use depends on record contents not fully specified in the prompt.

title: Provider can observe recurring backup communications and infer system activity
description: Nightly backup and replication traffic to the cloud provider reveals that the assignment and grading service is active and can expose timing, operational patterns, and likely existence of enrolled users and ongoing coursework through observed communication events.
uncertainty_note: The threat is grounded in observability of regular backup traffic; the precise extent of what can be inferred from traffic characteristics alone is context-dependent.

title: Full academic dataset is propagated to a third-party cloud provider
description: The flow sends full grade records, assignments, and the account directory to an external hosting provider. This propagation to another service expands exposure of personal data beyond the primary grading service and may exceed what is strictly necessary if more selective backup content or segregation could be used.

title: Backup includes an excessive amount of personal data
description: The description states that full records are shipped nightly, including grades, assignments, and the full account directory. Sending the complete dataset rather than a minimized or filtered backup may process more personal data than functionally needed for backup or replication purposes.
uncertainty_note: This assumes a minimized backup architecture could satisfy the operational need; some disaster-recovery designs may legitimately require full replicas.

title: Nightly full replication may process personal data more frequently than necessary
description: Performing full nightly backup and replication of the entire academic dataset may exceed the frequency needed for resilience objectives, especially if incremental backups or less frequent replication would suffice.
uncertainty_note: Need for nightly frequency depends on recovery-point objectives and service requirements, which are not provided.

title: Personal data is disclosed to a predetermined external party
description: The cloud hosting provider is a known third party that receives the backup dataset. Making full student academic and account data accessible to this external entity increases privacy exposure to an additional predetermined party.

title: Data subjects may be unaware their full educational records are replicated to a third-party host
description: Students and other data subjects may not reasonably expect that complete grade records, assignments, and account-directory data are transferred nightly to a third-party cloud hosting provider for backup and replication.
uncertainty_note: Whether users are actually unaware depends on privacy notices and internal communications, which are not given.

title: Third-party replication can hinder erasure or rectification across backups
description: When full records are replicated to an external provider, correcting or deleting personal data may become harder because the same data may persist in backup copies and replicated environments outside the primary service boundary.
uncertainty_note: Actual intervenability depends on backup-deletion and restoration procedures not described in the prompt.

title: Full backup replication risks violating data minimization
description: Shipping complete grade records, assignments, and the entire account directory to the cloud provider may involve more personal data than is necessary for the specific backup purpose, especially if selective, encrypted, or de-identified alternatives are feasible.
uncertainty_note: This is framed as a compliance risk; whether it is an actual violation depends on necessity, safeguards, and applicable legal basis.

title: Replication to external backup environments risks storage-limitation issues
description: Nightly backup and hosting replication to a third-party environment can create additional retained copies of educational records, increasing the risk that personal data is stored longer than necessary.
uncertainty_note: Retention periods are not specified, so this is a risk indicator rather than confirmed non-compliance.

title: Third-party transfer of student records may lack a clearly demonstrated lawful basis
description: Sending full academic and account-directory data to an external hosting provider for backup/replication introduces a lawfulness risk if the transfer, processor arrangement, or related safeguards are not properly established for this processing purpose.
uncertainty_note: The prompt does not state the applicable jurisdiction, contract terms, or lawful basis, so this is a plausible compliance threat rather than a confirmed violation.

title: Grade records can be linked across views via unique student identifiers
description: The grade records database likely stores records keyed by student identifiers so the grading service can assemble student, parent, and teacher views. Reuse of those identifiers across records and views creates a linking risk, enabling records about the same student to be connected across assignments, courses, and audiences.
uncertainty_note: The presence of unique student identifiers is strongly implied by the need to build multiple role-based views, but the exact identifier fields are not explicitly listed.

title: Grade records likely contain direct or persistent identifiers
description: To retrieve and present grade information for student, parent, and teacher views, the datastore likely provides records containing student IDs or similarly persistent references. Those identifiers make the data identifiable even if names are not always included in the flow.
uncertainty_note: The flow description does not enumerate fields, so this is based on the operational need to associate grades with specific students and related viewers.

title: Grade records can serve as attributable evidence about a student's performance
description: Stored grade records constitute attributable data that can be used to support claims about a student's submissions, performance, or academic status. Once read and used in views, these records may reduce the student's ability to deny the associated academic outcome.
uncertainty_note: This threat concerns attribution from the content of the grade record itself; no explicit signatures or metadata were described.

title: Building multiple role-based views may expose grade data to more predetermined parties than necessary
description: The grading service reads grade records in order to build student, parent, and teacher views. This means the same underlying personal data is made accessible to a fixed set of distinct parties. If the service reads or forwards full records without strict role-based minimization, disclosure risk arises because more parties receive the data than functionally necessary for each specific view.
uncertainty_note: The threat depends on whether the service minimizes data per audience; the description confirms multiple recipient roles but not the exact field-level filtering.

title: Students may be unaware that their grade records are reused to generate parent and teacher views
description: This flow explicitly reuses stored grade records to construct views for multiple audiences. Data subjects may not be aware of the full extent of this downstream processing and disclosure, particularly the generation of parent-facing and teacher-facing views from the same source records.
uncertainty_note: Awareness and notice mechanisms are not described, so this is a plausible transparency risk rather than a confirmed design flaw.

title: Role-based view generation may violate data minimization if full grade records are processed for each audience
description: The grading service reads grade records to build student, parent, and teacher views. If it processes full records for all audiences rather than only the minimum fields needed per role, the flow may conflict with the data minimization principle.
uncertainty_note: This is contingent on implementation details of the service's filtering and field selection, which are not provided.
